To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gendered analysis of the United Nations Security Council resolution 1325 reveals that the concept of gender as understood in policy making is limited and narrow, and that this impacts on the implementation of gender aware policies.

the concept of gender as it is understood in peacebuilding policy is narrow and limited to the inclusion of women in the formal political process, and that this narrow concept of gender is not in line with a more holistic and transformative approach to peacebuilding, which is needed to address the root causes of violence and build more sustainable peace.
the concept of gender in the context of peacebuilding policy needs to be understood within the context of the broader gendered relations of power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the implementation of SCR 1325 is contributing towards the building of a more positive peace, in the sense of a peace that is sustainable, just and inclusive of all.
how gender can contribute to a more positive understanding of peace and how the concept of peace can contribute to a better understanding of gender.
the question of how gendered understandings of peacebuilding can be developed to contribute to more effective policy and implementation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SCR 1325, in its present form, is not a sufficient vehicle for building a sustainable and positive peace, but that it does have the capacity to contribute to the development of a more transformative approach.

, in the absence of a more transformative approach, the implementation of the principles of SCR 1325 will continue to be limited and will fail to deliver on its promise of a more sustainable and positive form of peace.

the United Nations Security Council resolution 1325 (SCR 1325) on Women, Peace and Security is an important policy document that has the potential to make a significant impact on peacebuilding policy and practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the United Nations Security Council resolution 1325 (SCR 1325) has been critiquied in terms of its implemetation and there is a gap on the critical analysis concerning gender and the significant links between the constructs of gender and culture of violence and peace.
the gendered nature of peacebuilding policy is not well understood, and that this has implications for how the resolution is implemented.
we have found that the concept of gender in SCR 1325 is understood in a narrow and limited way and that this is a barrier to its effective implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a gendered analysis is necessary to build a more sustainable peace and to overcome the current inertia in the implementation of gender aware perspectives and gender sensitive policy in the peacebuilding arena.
gender is a complex concept that needs to be understood in a more nuanced way than the current policy approach.
a gendered analysis can provide a deeper understanding of the gendered nature of peacebuilding and how this can be used to build more sustainable peace.
